m66: 💡 Keep the sliced steak, rinsed soba and Nam Jim in three separate pots; the noodles and beef hold 3 days chilled, but dressed noodles turn slimy within hours.
💡 Toss the cold soba with a splash of water before boxing so the strands do not weld together, and eat the beef cold or barely warmed so medium-rare does not go grey.
m67: 💡 Grilled chicken with the yogurt dressing keeps 3 days refrigerated; slice the avocado on the day and pack the lettuce dry in its own container to stop it wilting.
💡 Take the chicken off the heat at 72°C and rest it covered for 5 minutes; it climbs to a safe 74°C without turning stringy.
m70: 💡 Sear the tenderloin to medium-rare only, cool it fast, and reheat slices for 60 seconds at 50% microwave power so the second cook does not push it past medium.
💡 Blanched asparagus and beans keep 3 days but soften in the microwave; a 3-minute toss in a hot pan revives them properly. The sweet potato freezes well on its own.
m71: 💡 Charred aubergine weeps liquid overnight, so drain it in a sieve before boxing and keep the mint-yogurt dressing in a separate lidded pot. The rice and beef freeze for 2 months.
💡 Sliced tenderloin dries out fast, so cook it just to pink and reheat the bowl covered at 70% power, stirring halfway, until the rice is steaming.
m72: 💡 Barramundi is best eaten within 2 days and does not freeze well once cooked; reheat in an air fryer at 160°C for 4 minutes to keep the skin crisp.
💡 Dry the scored skin thoroughly with kitchen paper and press the fillet flat with a spatula for the first 30 seconds so it does not curl and the skin renders evenly.
m73: 💡 The spinach rice keeps its colour for 4 days if cooled quickly and sealed; it freezes for 3 months, but the broccoli is better steamed fresh after reheating.
💡 Grill the chicken over medium-high rather than searing hot so the herb paste does not scorch before the centre reaches 74°C; slice against the grain for tender pieces.
m75: 💡 Box the mince and rice together for up to 4 days, but fry the egg fresh each morning; a reheated sunny-side egg turns rubbery and the yolk sets solid.
💡 Stir the Thai basil through only after the wok is off the heat; cooked too long it blackens and loses its aniseed flavour, so add a few fresh leaves when serving.
m76: 💡 Nasi goreng reheats well in a dry non-stick pan over high heat for 3 minutes, which restores the toasted grains far better than the microwave; keeps 4 days chilled.
💡 Cold day-old rice is non-negotiable here; freshly cooked rice steams rather than fries and turns to mush. Keep the crispy shallots and pickles in a separate pot.
m80: 💡 Store the cooked patties, buns and cottage-cheese sauce separately; patties keep 3 days and reheat in 2 minutes in a hot pan, while the blended sauce holds 4 days chilled.
💡 Smash the beef within the first 10 seconds while it is still cold and press hard once; after that leave it alone so the crust forms and the juices stay in the patty.
m81: 💡 Marinated grilled chicken keeps 4 days and freezes well; reheat in an air fryer at 170°C for 4 minutes, then add the bun, mozzarella and avo-mayo on the day.
💡 Pounding the breast to an even 2 cm means the thin edge does not dry out while the thick end catches up; the avo-mayo browns overnight, so mash it just before eating.
m82: 💡 The chopped chicken and egg mixture keeps 3 days in a sealed tub; toast the sourdough and spread the avocado only when serving or the bread goes soft and the avocado browns.
💡 Poach the chicken in barely simmering water, never a rolling boil, and pull it at 72°C to rest; boiled hard it turns chalky and the whole stack tastes dry.
m83: 💡 Grilled chicken keeps 4 days and freezes flat; pack the yogurt-garlic mayo, avocado and tomato in separate small pots and build the toastie fresh so the brioche stays crisp.
💡 A toasted brioche slice absorbs tomato juice in minutes, so lay the lettuce leaf against the bread as a barrier before the tomato and avocado go on.
m84: 💡 Assembled wraps keep 3 days chilled and reheat well in an air fryer at 180°C for 5 minutes, which re-crisps the tortilla; microwaving makes them limp.
💡 Cool the roasted sweet potato and broccoli fully before filling and spoon the yogurt dressing sparingly in the centre; hot vegetables steam the wrap and a wet filling leaks at the seam.
m85: 💡 Ten portions is a lot; refrigerate 5 days and freeze the rest for 3 months in single tubs, thawing overnight before reheating. Add a splash of milk or water to loosen the sauce.
💡 Pour the blended cheese sauce over pasta and beef off the heat; boiling a cottage-cheese sauce makes it grainy. Reheat covered at 60% power, stirring every minute, so it stays silky.
m86: 💡 Chickpea pasta softens noticeably by day 3, so undercook it by a minute at the start and reheat with a splash of water at 70% power for 2 to 3 minutes. Freezes for 2 months.
💡 Blend the cottage cheese for a full 2 minutes so it is completely smooth, then stir it in over low heat only; a fast simmer splits the sauce into curds.
bf33: 💡 Wrapped sandwiches keep 5 days chilled or freeze for 2 months; from frozen, unwrap and microwave 60 seconds, flip, then 60 more at full power, or bake 20 minutes at 175°C.
💡 Pull the egg bake as soon as the centre stops wobbling, around 20 minutes; overbaked egg goes rubbery on reheating. Wrap only once every layer is fully cool to prevent soggy muffins.
bf35: 💡 Cooled pancakes keep 4 days chilled or 2 months frozen between squares of baking paper; reheat in a toaster or air fryer at 160°C for 3 minutes rather than the microwave, which makes them gummy.
💡 Whey batter browns fast and stays raw inside if the pan is too hot, so keep the heat at medium and wait for bubbles to burst across the surface before flipping just once.
m88: 💡 Keeps 4 days in the fridge and the sauced chicken freezes for 2 months; jasmine rice reheats best with a tablespoon of water under a loose lid at full power for 2 minutes.
💡 The yogurt in the sauce may look speckled after baking, which is normal; scoring the breasts and pouring the sauce over them cold is what keeps the meat juicy through reheating.
m89: 💡 Pack the Greek yogurt and lime in a separate pot and reheat only the rice and steak; warmed yogurt goes watery and heated lime turns bitter. Bowls keep 4 days.
💡 Sear the sirloin to medium-rare rather than medium, since reheating cooks it further; slice thinly against the grain and warm for just 60 seconds at 50% power.
m90: 💡 Roasted salmon keeps 3 days but should not be frozen once cooked; reheat gently at 50% power for 90 seconds or eat it cold flaked over warm rice to avoid a dry fillet.
💡 Pull the fillets when the thickest part flakes but is still slightly translucent, around 15 minutes; they carry on cooking on the tray and again when reheated.
m91: 💡 Cooked prawns are safe 3 days chilled and taste better cold than reheated; if you must warm them, 40 seconds at 50% power is plenty before they turn rubbery.
💡 Keep cucumber, tomatoes and feta in a separate pot from the quinoa so their liquid does not soak in, and add the yogurt dressing at the table. Do not freeze this one.
m92: 💡 Keeps 4 days chilled and the chicken freezes for 3 months; the jasmine rice reheats fluffy with a splash of water, covered, at full power for 2 minutes with a stir halfway.
💡 Resting the baked breasts 5 minutes before slicing keeps the juices in the meat; cut too early and the chicken dries out by day 2. Save the final lemon squeeze for serving.
m93: 💡 Boiled baby potatoes go mealy in the freezer, so keep this to 4 days chilled; reheat the potatoes and beef at full power for 2 minutes with the mozzarella on top so it melts.
💡 Put the Greek yogurt dollop in a separate mini pot and add it after reheating; warmed yogurt splits, and drain the corn thoroughly or it waters down the taco beef.
m94: 💡 Reheat in a dry non-stick pan for 3 to 4 minutes on high, pressing the rice flat for the last minute to bring back the crust; keeps 4 days chilled and freezes for 2 months.
💡 Do not skip chilling the rice uncovered for at least an hour; warm rice steams and clumps. Scramble the eggs only until barely set, since they cook again on reheating.
m95: 💡 Keeps 4 days in the fridge and the sauced chicken freezes for 3 months; broccoli softens in the freezer, so add a fresh handful when reheating at 70% power for 3 minutes.
💡 The honey sauce burns at the edges of the dish if the chicken is crowded, so use a tray where the breasts sit in a single layer and baste once at 20 minutes.
m96: 💡 Jars keep 4 days chilled, but the cucumber and tomatoes weep, so put the tzatziki at the bottom and the chicken and chickpeas on top, then tip out to mix when eating.
💡 If the rotisserie chicken is already 2 days old, use the jars within 2 days rather than 4; cooked chicken counts its shelf life from when it was first cooked.
m97: 💡 Refrigerates 5 days and freezes 3 months; defrost overnight and reheat covered at 70% power with a tablespoon of water so the mozzarella melts rather than turning to leather.
💡 Stir the cottage cheese in off the boil and let it melt from residual heat; if the passata is bubbling hard the curds tighten into grains instead of turning silky.
m98: 💡 This bowl is best eaten within 3 days; rest the steak, slice it thin, and reheat everything except the herb yogurt sauce at 60% power for 90 seconds.
💡 Pat the sirloin bone-dry before it hits the pan; a damp surface steams instead of searing and you lose the crust in a non-stick pan with no oil.
m99: 💡 Eat within 2 days and skip the freezer; reheat the rice and broccoli first, then rest the salmon on top so it warms through gently rather than being blasted.
💡 Bake the fillet on foil with the lemon added only in the last 5 minutes; a long acid soak firms the outer flesh and leaves it dry by the second day.
m100: 💡 Rice, chicken and beans keep 4 days and freeze for 2 months; the yogurt, lime and any salsa go in a separate pot so they stay cool while the rest reheats.
💡 Dice the chicken after resting, not before cooking; small raw cubes dry out in a hot pan, whereas a whole breast browned 5 minutes per side stays moist.
m101: 💡 Best eaten fresh, but it keeps 2 days chilled; the cottage cheese sauce sets when cold, so reheat with a tablespoon of water at 60% power and stir well.
💡 Keep the pot on the lowest heat when adding the cottage cheese; if the pasta is scorching hot the sauce turns grainy, and add the tomatoes last so they warm without collapsing.
m102: 💡 Keeps 3 days chilled and freezes for 1 month; the macaroni soaks up the sauce, so reheat with a splash of milk or water at 70% power, stirring every minute.
💡 Melt the mozzarella and cottage cheese over low heat with the pasta water before adding the buffalo sauce; vinegar-based hot sauce added to a boiling dairy sauce makes it split.
m103: 💡 Keeps 4 days but does not freeze well; the blended cottage-cheese sauce tightens when cold, so loosen each portion with 2 tablespoons of water before microwaving at 70% power.
💡 Blend the sauce until completely smooth, at least 2 minutes, and toss it through the pasta while warm but off the heat so it stays creamy rather than grainy.
v10: 💡 Keeps 4 days chilled; the baked tofu reheats brilliantly in an air fryer at 180°C for 4 minutes, which restores the chew, while the quinoa can go in the microwave.
💡 Press the tofu for the full 20 minutes and lay the cubes without touching; crowded, damp tofu steams on the tray and never turns golden, and it freezes poorly once cooked.
v11: 💡 Keeps 3 days but hold the peanut sauce in a separate jar until eating; dressed soba soaks it up and the cabbage wilts, so toss each portion just before serving.
💡 Rinse the soba under cold running water and rub the strands to wash off surface starch; skip this and they clump into a solid block by the next morning.
